You: I caught a huge tilapia recently. Did you see it?
Mrs. Fisher: Huge tilapia, huh.
You: You don’t sound very impressed.
Mrs. Fisher: Well, tilapia is like…{{wi}} a water rat.
You: Water rat?
Mrs. Fisher: It eats the worst kind of things in the water. Animal poop, algae and even industrial waste. Thanks to it the water is cleaner, but it is an invasive species. The taste isn’t bad, but the poop eating just doesn’t sit well with me. A lot of mixed feelings.
You: I didn’t know that. Are they unhealthy?
Mrs. Fisher: They should be fine to eat, but I personally would stick to the tilapias from the fish farm. The water there is much cleaner than in other places.
You: Got it.
Mrs. Fisher: Tilapia is the most farmed fish in the world. It’s resistant to disease, doesn’t mind polluted water or heavily overcrowded farms and these harsh conditions do not impact the taste of the fish. 
Mrs. Fisher: If you want some, get it from a good source.
